The part is the channel fixture's faces exported as a shell-based surface model, with no solid. Python's recess families scan such a part as one source (`solids or [part]`, a documented record-only open-shell compatibility input) and publish the fixture's channel with body_key null; the port reads the faces without a solid and, like every ported family, scans solids only, so it finds nothing. Python's void proof there is vacuous (its probe intersects a box with a shell, which has no volume), so porting the path faithfully would publish recesses without a material proof; whether surface models should be recognised at all is a maintainer question. Python's evidence path refuses this part (no valid solid), as the port does.
